items.title: Rectangular grid and Dirichlet flux stencil
items.statement: Define the rectangular grid, grid inner product and real divergence-form Dirichlet operator with exact midpoint face coefficients; the constant-coefficient case is the five-point Laplacian.

references.title: Endre Süli, Numerical Solution of PDEs, complete lecture notes
Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 5: Finite Difference Approximation
Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 6: General Linear Second Order Equation

items.title: Discrete summation by parts, Poincaré inequality and inverse bound
items.statement: The rectangular grid operator satisfies a boundary-term summation-by-parts identity; zero-boundary grid functions satisfy a mesh-uniform discrete Poincaré inequality, and the positive-coefficient operator has a mesh-uniform inverse bound in the weighted grid L2 norm.
items.strategy: Direct telescoping on horizontal and vertical edges, followed by a one-direction discrete Poincaré estimate and coercivity.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; only finite sums and finite-dimensional linear algebra are used.

items.title: Second-order consistency of the variable-coefficient flux stencil
items.statement: For a positive scalar coefficient in C3 and a solution in C4 on a rectangle, exact midpoint face coefficients in the divergence-form stencil have a second-order interior residual with an explicit derivative bound.
items.strategy: Expand each face coefficient and one-sided difference through second order; the common quadratic flux term cancels between adjacent faces.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; the proof uses pointwise Taylor estimates.

items.title: Second-order grid L2 error for rectangular Dirichlet flux differences
items.statement: For a C3 uniformly positive scalar coefficient and a C4 solution of the Dirichlet problem on a rectangle, the exact-boundary divergence-form finite-difference solution is unique and its weighted grid L2 error is bounded explicitly by a constant times hx2+hy2.
items.strategy: Apply the discrete inverse bound to the complete interior residual; exact Dirichlet boundary rows make the boundary error zero.
items.axiom_base: No choice axiom is used; existence and uniqueness are proved by finite-dimensional coercivity.

items.title: A one-sided Neumann closure gives only first-order error
items.statement: For u(x)=x2 on [0,1], the centered interior Poisson stencil with the one-sided left Neumann row D+U0=0 and exact right Dirichlet value has grid error h(1-xi), so its maximum error is h.
items.strategy: Compute the one-sided boundary residual and solve the homogeneous interior error recurrence with the right endpoint condition.

items.title: A Dirichlet Laplacian inverse is uniformly bounded in the maximum norm
items.statement: For the one-dimensional centered Dirichlet Laplacian on [0,1], the induced maximum-norm operator bound satisfies ||A_N^{-1}||infinity-to-infinity <= 1/8 for every mesh width h=1/N.
items.strategy: Use a quadratic barrier and the discrete minimum principle to bound both signs of the solution.

items.title: Flux and expanded variable-coefficient stencils differ by a second-order term
items.statement: For a(x,y)=1+x2 and u(x,y)=x2 on (0,1)2, the midpoint divergence-form x-flux and the independently expanded centered operator differ by exactly hx2/2 at every interior grid point.
items.strategy: Evaluate the two midpoint face fluxes and compare them with a_i delta2_x u+a_x D0_x u.

items.title: The five-point Laplacian is exact on a quadratic solution
items.statement: For u(x,y)=x2+y2 on a rectangle with exact sampled Dirichlet data and f=-4, the five-point scheme returns the exact grid samples on every rectangular uniform grid.
items.strategy: Compute the central second differences exactly and use the zero-boundary uniqueness estimate.
